stem: A hospital uses the National Database of Nursing Quality Indicators (NDNQI) to review nursing performance. What is a key value of this database?

options.A: It replaces the hospital's internal quality-improvement work
options.B: It allows comparison of nursing performance with external benchmarks to identify improvement opportunities
options.C: It collects nursing data without supporting performance improvement
options.D: It tracks only financial performance rather than nursing-sensitive measures

rationale: The current NDNQI program provides nursing-quality data and benchmarking so organizations can compare performance across facilities and nursing units and use those insights to improve quality. Benchmarking complements, rather than replaces, local quality-improvement work. B is correct.
educational_objective: Explain how external nursing-quality benchmarking supports local quality-improvement efforts.
source_document_title: National Database of Nursing Quality Indicators (NDNQI)
source_locator: NDNQI — Benchmark nursing performance; See how you stack up / Benchmark your performance
source_claim_supported: NDNQI allows healthcare organizations to compare nursing performance across facilities and units using nursing-sensitive measures and benchmarking data to support improvement.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Management of Care — quality improvement and performance evaluation
blueprint_topic: Management of Care — benchmarking and nursing quality improvement

source_original.stem: A hospital participates in the National Database of Nursing Quality Indicators (NDNQI) to benchmark its nurse-sensitive outcomes against other facilities, and a new manager assumes this data mainly just sits in a report with no real follow-up. The purpose of this participation is instead to:

options.A: Replace internal quality-improvement work because national benchmark reports are sufficient
options.B: Compare unit outcomes with national benchmarks to identify gaps and guide improvement efforts
options.C: Collect nursing data without using it to change practice, staffing, education, or safety processes
options.D: Track financial performance only rather than clinically relevant nurse-sensitive outcomes

source_original.rationale: Participation in a national nursing quality database such as NDNQI allows hospitals to compare their unit-level nurse-sensitive outcome data against national benchmarks, helping identify specific areas for improvement, track progress over time, and support evidence-based nursing quality initiatives.
source_original.source_detail: NDNQI benchmarking: unit-level nurse-sensitive outcomes compared with national benchmarks for quality improvement; reviewed 2026-08-14.

correction_summary: Updated the source to the current NDNQI owner/program page at Press Ganey, removed manager cueing, and avoided overclaiming that benchmark data alone changes staffing or practice. Difficulty reduced from hard to medium.

audit_findings.source_authority: Current NDNQI program page; NCSBN 2026 blueprint
audit_findings.currentness: Current Press Ganey NDNQI page checked 2026-08-17.
audit_findings.claim_audit: NDNQI's stated purpose includes comparing performance across thousands of facilities/units and using nursing-sensitive measures to improve quality.

distractor_audit.A: External benchmarking does not replace local QI.
distractor_audit.D: NDNQI focuses on nursing-quality performance, not only finance.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: B is uniquely consistent with current program description.
audit_findings.cueing: Removed narrative assumption and simplified choices.
audit_findings.blueprint: Quality improvement and performance evaluation fit Management of Care.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Rechecked current NDNQI page; B remains uniquely correct.
